name: Na'ahai
world_status: a description exists but is not accessible

sources.citation: Tryon, Darrell T. 1976. New Hebrides languages: an internal classification (PL C-50). Canberra: Pacific Linguistics. Malfaxal wordlist (language no. 116/118)
sources.note: Comparative wordlists and sound-correspondence tables only; no per-language stress statement for Malfaxal.

sources.citation: Rangelov, Tihomir, Mary Walworth & Julie Barbour. 2023. A multifaceted approach to understanding unexpected sound change: the bilabial trills of Vanuatu's Malekula Island. Diachronica (accepted MS, Waikato Research Commons hdl:10289/15510)
sources.note: Nothing on Na'ahai stress. Its source appendix lists the only phonological sources for Na'ahai (malf1237) as Maddieson (1989:94) [article] and Anastasia Riehl (p.c. 2019) — i.e. no published grammar or phonology exists as of 2023.

sources.citation: Shimelman, Aviva, Paul Heggarty et al. 2019-2025. Vanuatu Voices / Sound Comparisons 'Vanuatu' word lists, CLDF dataset lexibank/vanuatuvoices (4 Na'ahai varieties: Toman Island, Mbatvanui, Malfaxal, Mbatmbang; 725 forms, recorded by A. Shimelman, transcribed by L. Wägerle)
sources.note: Wordlist only; transcriptions are broad segmental IPA with no stress marks (0 of 725 Na'ahai forms carry ˈ); silent on stress.

sources.citation: Riehl, Anastasia. 2015. Initial Documentation of Na'ahai, a language of Malakula, Vanuatu. Endangered Languages Archive, deposit 0245. hdl:2196/00-0000-0000-000F-780A-1 (deposit landing page and full bundle list, 2 pages)
sources.note: Deposit blurb states the collection includes 'a grammatical sketch covering phonology through discourse structure', a dictionary and literacy materials, but the 41 visible bundles are all narrative/song recordings (subscriber access) plus a cover image; no sketch or dictionary bundle is listed, so nothing on stress could be read.

sources.citation: Lynch, John. 2014. Unexpected final vowel retention in Malakula. Open Linguistics 1: 1-16. doi:10.2478/opli-2014-0001 (Wayback copy of De Gruyter PDF)
sources.access_detail: copy on file; access check: open copy online (also: harvard online access (harvardkey); publisher (doi, likely paywalled))
sources.note: Nothing. Naha'ai (=Malfaxal) appears only in subgrouping discussion and cognate tables; the word 'stress' does not occur in the paper.

sources.citation: Dimock, Laura Gail. 2009. A grammar of Nahavaq (Malakula, Vanuatu). PhD thesis, Victoria University of Wellington. doi:10.26686/wgtn.16968481
sources.note: Grammar of the neighbouring language Nahavaq (sout2857), not Na'ahai. Mentions Na'ahai for intelligibility, loans and sources (Maddieson 1989a:94-95 on trills; 'Anastasia Riehl (University of Toronto) working on Na'ahai'); no statement about Na'ahai stress.

sources.citation: Curtis, Tim. 2002. Talking about place: identities, histories and powers among the Na'hai speakers of Malakula (Vanuatu). PhD thesis, Australian National University. hdl:1885/10717
sources.note: Nothing on word stress; ethnography. p.3 only notes Na'hai is spoken on Tomman (Ur), Milip, Bwad-Bang and 'with a notably different accent in Malfakhal and Mbonvor' (dialect accent, not word accent).

sources.citation: Lynch, John & Terry Crowley. 2001. Languages of Vanuatu: A new survey and bibliography (PL 517). Canberra: Pacific Linguistics. Sec. 3.7.4 Naha'ai, p.74
sources.access_detail: copy on file; access check: open copy online: WID Offsite Storage PL6211.V36 L96 2001
sources.note: Bibliographic survey: the only sources for Naha'ai are Tryon (1976) short vocabulary, Charpentier (1982b) vocabulary, Curtis (1999) ritual terms; nothing on stress.

sources.citation: Riehl, Anastasia. [2008-2009]. Grammatical sketch of Na'ahai ('covering phonology through discourse structure') and Na'ahai dictionary, prepared for ELDP project PPG0047 'Initial Documentation of Na'ahai, a language of Malakula, Vanuatu'; described in ELAR deposit 0245 (Riehl 2015, hdl:2196/00-0000-0000-000F-780A-1) but not among the listed bundles. Author now at Strathy Language Unit, Queen's University (Kingston, Ontario).
sources.tag: wanted: likely states stress, not held
sources.note: The only first-hand description of Na'ahai phonology known to exist (ELAR blurb; Dimock 2009 fn.3; Rangelov et al. 2023 cite Riehl p.c. as their Na'ahai source); would contain the stress statement if anyone has written one.

sources.citation: Lynch, John. 2016. Malakula internal subgrouping: phonological evidence. Oceanic Linguistics 55(2): 399-431.
sources.tag: wanted: likely states stress, not held
sources.access_detail: online with a Harvard login (also: harvard online access (harvardkey); publisher (doi, likely paywalled))
sources.note: Comparative-historical phonology of all Malakula languages including Naha'ai; may contain general remarks on (penultimate) stress and vowel loss relevant to South Malakula, though any Na'ahai-specific statement would be second-hand.

sources.citation: Maddieson, Ian. 1989. Aerodynamic constraints on sound change: the case of bilabial trills. UCLA Working Papers in Phonetics 72: 91-115 (Na'ahai pp. 94-95).

sources.access_detail: open copy online, not fetched sources
sources.note: Only published phonetic study using Na'ahai recordings (11 words); narrow transcriptions might mark stress, but the topic is trills — low expected yield.

sources.citation: Charpentier, Jean-Michel. 1982. Atlas linguistique du Sud-Malakula / Linguistic atlas of South Malakula (Vanuatu). Vol. 1 (introduction, 177 pp.) + Vol. 2 (maps). Paris: SELAF / Langues et cultures du Pacifique.

sources.note: The most extensive lexical source for Na'ahai (Naha'ai/Nahaxai dialects); vol. 1 introduction may state transcription conventions for stress or give per-language phonological notes (French/English).
